titulo: Ser, pronouns and adjectives: Pronouns and the verb ser

aula.objetivo: Use subject pronouns and the present tense of «ser», make the adjective agree in gender and number, negate with «no», say your profession and ask simple questions with «ser».

blocos.titulo: Un grupo nuevo / A new group
blocos.contexto: Ana meets Luis, Marta and Pablo. Listen without reading the text and notice the words «soy», «eres», «es», «somos» and «son». They're today's topic.

linhas.ru: — Yo soy Luis. Ella es Marta.
linhas.audio: Yo soy Luis. Ella es Marta.

linhas.pt: — Nice to meet you, Marta. Who's he?

linhas.ru: — Él es Pablo. Pablo y Luis son amigos.
linhas.pt: — He's Pablo. Pablo and Luis are friends.
linhas.audio: Él es Pablo. Pablo y Luis son amigos.

linhas.pt: — Yes, we're friends. And you two? Are you friends?

linhas.ru: — Sí, Marta y yo somos amigas.
linhas.pt: — Yes, Marta and I are friends.
linhas.audio: Sí, Marta y yo somos amigas.

itens.pt: you all (formal; in Latin America, everyone)

blocos.titulo: Subject pronouns and the present of ser
blocos.explicacao: You just heard «soy», «es», «somos» and «son». Now the rule, in short steps. STEP 1: «ser» is the verb for saying who someone is, where they're from, what their profession is, and what they're like. The present tense is irregular: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son. STEP 2: the verb already shows the person, so the subject pronoun is almost always left out: «Soy Ana», not «Yo soy Ana». You use the pronoun to contrast or emphasize: «Yo soy Ana y ella es Marta.» STEP 3: «tú» (informal) takes «eres»; «usted» (formal) takes the same form as «él» and «ella»: «Usted es médico.» STEP 4: in the plural, «nosotros» takes «somos»; «ellos» and «ellas» take «son»; «ustedes» also takes «son». STEP 5: «vosotros» takes «sois» and is used only in Spain. It doesn't exist in Latin America: people say «ustedes son», for everyone. In Argentina and some Central American countries you'll also hear «vos sos» instead of «tú eres». STEP 6: there are feminine forms: «nosotras», «vosotras», «ellas». A mixed group uses the masculine. STEP 7: there's no required dummy subject like English «it»: you say «Es tarde» (it's late), with no subject at all. STEP 8: the accent mark matters: «él» (he) has an accent; «el» (the) doesn't. «Tú» (you) has an accent; «tu» (your) doesn't.
blocos.comparacao: English «to be» also changes with the person (am/is/are), but English almost always keeps the subject pronoun («I am», «you are»); Spanish usually drops it, since the verb ending already says who. The forms look a little like «to be» in sound, but don't map one-to-one: «soy» = I am, «eres» = you are (informal), «es» = he/she/it is or formal you are, «somos» = we are, «son» = they are or formal you-all are.

erros.motivo: «Usted» takes the same form as «él» and «ella».
As a pronoun, «tú» carries an accent; without it, «tu» means «your».

blocos.enunciado: First, say your own name out loud: «Soy…». Then introduce three people you know: «Ella es… Él es… Ellos son amigos.» Finally, say all six forms of «ser» in a row, without the pronouns: «soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son».
Review lesson 1 out loud: greet someone with «tú» and with «usted». Then read: jamón, gente, queso, zapato, calle, niño, perro, hotel.
